headline: CISA flags four exploited enterprise flaws as Microsoft breach and GPGME bug sharpen risk
standfirst: CISA’s addition of four enterprise flaws to its known-exploited catalog leads a day of active-exploitation reports, a suspected AI-agent intrusion into medical-imaging infrastructure, a Microsoft identity-data breach, a reported FBI database compromise, a critical GPGME bug, a ransomware-recovery fraud case and new research on Com vishing and BADBOX ad fraud.
bodyMarkdown:
## Actively exploited

CISA added four flaws affecting Apache Roller, Cisco Expressway, SAP NetWeaver and Broadcom VMware vCenter to KEV, citing evidence of active exploitation [[s9]]. The enriched record is CVE-2026-129448, a critical 9.8 deserialization bug in Apache Roller 4.0 through before 6.1.5; NVD says an unauthenticated remote attacker can execute arbitrary code through the XML-RPC endpoint before authentication. CISA’s required action is tied to federal guidance, not a universal deadline, and the record does not establish ransomware use.

A threat-intelligence report states that suspected China-linked hackers used autonomous AI agents to find a zero-day in MONAI Label and gain root on a university server [[s7]]. The flaw lets an attacker with no account write files outside the server’s storage folder; it affects MONAI Label 0.8.5 and earlier in the default setup. The attribution remains suspected, and no CVE was supplied.

Microsoft says it suffered a data breach after attackers exploited a vulnerability in Entra Connect Health, exposing administrator email addresses and tenant configuration information [[s1]]. No CVE, affected versions or remediation were supplied. Analysis: the exposed tenant configuration could help attackers map identity trust, though the excerpt does not describe follow-on abuse.

## Breaches

The FBI has reportedly been breached for the second time in two months, with the latest incident targeting the National Crime Information Center, the cross-agency law enforcement data-sharing system [[s3]]. The report is unconfirmed in the supplied excerpt, and no scope, attacker or data impact was provided.

## Vulnerabilities

The GnuPG project warned that CVE-2026-129975, a critical memory bug in GPGME, can be triggered by a malicious OpenPGP key with an unusually long user ID and could steal data from affected applications [[s6]]. All software using GPGME before 2.3.0 is affected, and fixed versions are available. The CVE has no KEV match in the supplied intelligence; that is a catalog miss, not evidence that exploitation has not occurred.

## Industry

The CTO and co-founder of ransomwarehelp.com has been indicted for wire fraud after an FBI sting found the recovery service was paying attackers for decryption keys and charging victims a markup for work never performed [[s10]]. Analysis: the case is a cautionary tale about recovery vendors whose claims outrun their technical work.

## Research

A new analysis maps how Com affiliates blend vishing, cloud data theft and extortion against healthcare and finance, with defense guidance [[s11]]. Analysis: the TTP detail is the useful part for defenders facing social-engineering-led cloud intrusions.

BADBOX malware in generic Android TV boxes has returned to large-scale ad fraud after last year’s disruptions, with 40 billion daily ad requests [[s2]]. Analysis: the reported volume suggests the botnet remains durable despite prior disruption efforts.

kev.vulnerabilityName: Apache Roller Deserialization of Untrusted Data Vulnerability
kev.shortDescription: Apache Roller contains a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code via the XML-RPC endpoint, which accepts and deserializes vendor extension types before authentication. This CVE covers the same underlying vulnerability as CVE-2026-82384 but applies to a broader range of affected versions.
kev.requiredAction: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.

nvd.description:
Deserialization of Untrusted Data in Apache Roller versions 4.0.0 through 6.1.4 allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code. The XML-RPC endpoint accepts vendor extension types and deserializes them before authenticating the requester.

This is the same vulnerability as CVE-2026-82384, which listed only Apache Roller 6.1.5 as affected. This issue is being actively exploited.

Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.6 or later, which disables the extension types and rejects XML-RPC requests when the XML-RPC feature is disabled.

Users who cannot upgrade right away should set "enabledForExtensions" to "false" in WEB-INF/web.xml, or remove the "/roller-services/xmlrpc" servlet mapping, and restart Roller. Disabling XML-RPC in the administration UI is not enough, because older versions deserialize the request before checking that setting.

selected.angle: CISA KEV additions confirm active exploitation of multiple enterprise flaws across Apache Roller, Cisco Expressway, SAP NetWeaver and VMware vCenter, with a near-term federal patch deadline.

selected.title: GnuPG Warns Critical GPGME Flaw Could Expose App Data via Malicious OpenPGP Keys
selected.excerpt: A malicious OpenPGP key with an unusually long user ID can trigger a critical memory bug in GPGME, the standard library that programs use to work with GnuPG. The GnuPG project warned yesterday that the flaw could be used to steal data from affected applications and has released fixed versions. The bug, tracked as CVE-2026-129975, affects all software that uses GPGME before version 2.3.0,
selected.angle: A critical GPGME memory bug reachable via a malicious OpenPGP key puts applications that parse untrusted keys at risk, and fixed versions are available.

selected.title: CTO of ‘RansomwareHelp’ Indicted for Wire Fraud
selected.excerpt: The chief technology officer and co-founder of ransomwarehelp.com, a six year old Florida business that claimed to use "advanced cryptographic tools" to restore data locked by ransomware, has been charged with wire fraud after an FBI sting operation found the company was simply paying the attackers for a decryption key and charging victims a markup for work that was never performed.
selected.angle: The indictment turns a ransomware recovery service into a cautionary tale about firms that allegedly paid attackers and charged victims a markup for work never performed.
